item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports finer matching, but several close matches violate the no-pretrained-model constraint. [MARS (CIKM 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) learns multiple attribute-aware user/item representations and scores attribute-wise interactions, offering an architectural precedent for preserving distinct interests rather than compressing everything into one vector; its text pipeline uses pretrained language models. [FineRec (SIGIR 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12975) builds attribute-specific graphs from review attribute–opinion pairs extracted by an LLM, making its pipeline unsuitable when reviews and pretrained models are unavailable. [C-TLSAN (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13021) integrates product-description content into long- and short-term attention, supporting content–temporal fusion, though its abstract does not establish a text encoder trained from scratch.\n\nThe clearest candidate-conditioned precedent found is older: [Multi-Level Interaction Reranking (2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.09370) explicitly models candidate–history and feature-level interactions with personalized long-/short-term attention. Practical adaptation, proposed here rather than established by these papers: retain SASRec and add candidate-query attention over historical collaborative embeddings, plus a separate title/description matching branch using TF-IDF or trainable token embeddings. Combine maximum, recency-weighted and attention-pooled similarities through a small gated scoring head; ablate collaborative-only, text-only and combined variants using the fixed macro validation HR@10. This search did not establish a directly matching 2024–2026 method combining candidate-conditioned history matching with scratch-trained text. Metadata overlap supplies relevance evidence, but cannot establish ownership, compatibility or satisfied demand."}
